content.rendered:
“Wooly Bully” is a rock/Tex-Mex hybrid released in 1964 by novelty act Sam the Sham and the Pharoahs. It became a massive hit the following year, earning Billboard Magazine’s Number One Record of the Year distinction.

Bruce has covered it sixteen times over the years, unsurprisingly since he once proclaimed that “any bar band worth its salt has got to know this one.” Here’s what I think is their best take, from Tacoma in 1984.

Bonus footage: check out this high-quality video from the original artists.

Wooly Bully
First performed: September 19, 1982 (Asbury Park, NJ)
Last performed: May 8, 2009 (University Park, PA)

March 31, 2018

excerpt.rendered: As Bruce once put it, “any bar band worth its salt has got to know this one.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: Kingdom of Days: December 5
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: President Obama and an all-star line-up of musicians pay tribute to Bruce at the Kennedy Center Honors. Video and more highlights from this date in Springsteen history inside.

jetpack-related-posts.title: October 19
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On this date: Rosie goes missing, Queen of the Supermarket turns up, Philly Elvis makes his debut, and more. Plus: highlights from the star-studded Alliance of Neighbors benefit concert.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Wild Thing
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: The E Street Band refuses to be stumped when a fan requests The Troggs' bar band classic.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Tell Him
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: In 1984, a redheaded woman walked into a bar and changed the course of Bruce Springsteen's life. This is the song she sang, and their only circulating performance of it together.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Got to Get You Off My Mind
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: When Southside Johnny took ill, Bruce, Steve, the E Street Band, and the Jukes came to the rescue. From May 1977, here's one of Bruce's only performances of the Solomon Burke classic.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Crying in the Chapel
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One time only: Bruce backs a special Wonder Bar house band of local legends on a cover of Darrell Glenn's classic "Crying in the Chapel."
